- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., -0.4 → +0.3), model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment shift.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion: if price is 3–5% above 30-day moving avg, forecast often stays above; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; dampen first 3–5 forecast points by 0.5–1.0%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.3 → +0.2 → -0.4), model misreads momentum; apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average before forecasting.
